rule: GOAL: Fill the middle row of dots to match the color sequence shown at the top of the screen. CONTROLS: Click a colored button at the bottom to select it, then click an empty dot in the middle to place that color. Press SPACE to confirm your solution. RULE: Each color can be used only once; selecting a button moves that color out of the bottom row and into the selected dot. TRAP: Believing you must click buttons in a specific order; actually, you can select any available color and place it in any empty slot independently.

GOAL: Align the blue bar beneath the magenta shooter to catch the beam. CONTROLS: Arrows move the blue bar; Space fires the beam. RULE: The beam travels straight down, so the bar must cover the shooter's column. TRAP: Thinking the bar changes color due to beam contact; it was just a screen-wide flash effect.

GOAL: Slide across the ice to reach the green exit tile. CONTROLS: Arrow keys push the character until they hit a wall or obstacle. RULE: You cannot stop mid-slide; you must land exactly on the goal or pass over it if allowed. TRAP: Trying to navigate around corners fails because you slide straight through open spaces without stopping.

GOAL: Move the purple token along the dotted trail to reach the bubble. CONTROLS: Click on a trail dot to jump the token there; clicking elsewhere does nothing. RULE: You can only move up to three waypoints ahead in a single click. TRAP: Assuming you could click the final bubble directly or move more than three steps at once.

GOAL: Align the wedge between the interlocking white regions to fit the gap. CONTROLS: The upper blue button pushed the wedge right; the lower blue button pulled it left. RULE: Moving the wedge shifted the boundary, expanding one white region while contracting the other. TRAP: Believing the arrow was a cursor to select a target, rather than a physical plug to be shifted.

GOAL: Fit the arch piece into the cup by moving it down. CONTROLS: Click glyph bars and stems to set direction; click the ball to run. RULE: Two bottom bars signal a downward move; five moves reach the target depth. TRAP: Believing the arch needs horizontal alignment; it only requires vertical descent.

GOAL: Shrink the oversized knob by matching a pattern, then slide it left to the handle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the knob; clicks on the side panel set the pattern. RULE: Matching the target pattern shrinks the knob to 2x2, allowing it to fit through narrow gaps. TRAP: Assuming the knob stays small; successful pattern matches toggle size, so avoid extra matches after shrinking.

GOAL: Fill the frame with two chips. CONTROLS: Arrows move the head; Space absorbs or deposits a chip directly in front. RULE: The carried chip always sits in the socket opposite your facing direction. TRAP: Believing the chip stays still during turns; it swings to the new front when you rotate.

GOAL: Shrink the four-by-four block to two-by-two, then slide it up the shaft to reach the top. CONTROLS: Click matching colors to shrink; use arrows to move the block two spaces per press. RULE: The narrow gate only fits when the block aligns perfectly with the opening columns. TRAP: Assuming the block moves one space per arrow press wastes time; it shifts two spaces, requiring careful parity checks.

GOAL: Slide the arrow right until its tail aligns with the matching green gap in the lower bar. CONTROLS: The B-pair sliders moved the arrow; the A-pair sliders were inactive for this specific alignment task. RULE: Only the arrow connected to the same color as the gap could be moved into position. TRAP: Assuming both slider pairs affected the arrow wasted time; only the B-pair actually shifted the piece.

GOAL: Match the color sequence to the two target boxes. CONTROLS: Click tiles to swap their positions. RULE: Read the grid in two-by-two blocks from left to right, top then bottom. TRAP: Assuming a simple left-to-right row reading ignores the block structure, causing mismatches after the first pair.

GOAL: Navigate the corridor to the exit without touching the moving hazard. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player one step in the chosen direction. RULE: The red block only chases you if you share its exact row. TRAP: Believing proximity alone triggers the chase; vertical distance is safe.

ESTABLISHED: The arm extends to touch blocks but never pushes or pulls them. FAILED: Trying to move blocks by extending the arm into their cells. GOAL IS NOT: A mechanic involving pushing or dragging blocks with the arm. CONTROLS: Extending moves the tip; blocks stay put unless touched, where the arm stops.

ESTABLISHED: The puzzle requires matching rotated partner tiles to specific alphabet glyphs. The rotation transformation is fixed and deterministic. FAILED: Trying to use orientation alone to disambiguate between similar glyphs without calculating the exact transform failed. GOAL IS NOT: The goal is not merely matching any similar shape, but achieving the exact rotated glyph alignment. CONTROLS: UP presses advance the glyph cycle; rotation transforms map positions to determine the required target shape.

GOAL: Fill the blue container by placing the M and b pieces into its empty slots. CONTROLS: Click a tray piece to select it, click a container slot to drop it, and press Space to submit the solution. RULE: Only one piece can be held at a time; clicking a new tray button while holding a piece does nothing. TRAP: Thinking you can queue pieces by clicking multiple tray buttons, which caused wasted clicks and placement errors.

GOAL: Clear the path by capturing three guards and reaching the exit without dying. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step; moving into a guard removes it; reaching the goal wins. RULE: Guards only attack if you are exactly two steps away in the direction they face. TRAP: Thinking guards block movement like walls; they do not, allowing you to pass through or capture them freely if out of range.

GOAL: Rotate each column so the pink shape matches the blue partner, applying the same transform used by the blue pair. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shifted the vertical position of the tiles within their respective columns. RULE: The required orientation for the pink shape depended entirely on the specific transformation linking the two blue shapes in that column. TRAP: Assuming the pink shape needed to match the blue shape directly, rather than applying the intermediate rotation or flip observed between the blue pair.

GOAL: Place the hollow port piece and fill six empty slots so the reading order matches the target colors. CONTROLS: Click a tray item, then a slot to place it; press space to check. RULE: Reading the red row left to right, the port inserts its connected green box’s slots at that exact spot. TRAP: Believing the port is just another color slot; it is a structural connector that shifts the sequence order.

GOAL: Match three colored plunger tails to specific vertical gaps. CONTROLS: Click columns to raise or lower white bars, adjusting plunger heights. RULE: A bar cannot grow higher than the lowest top of its neighboring walls. TRAP: Assuming any wall limits growth; the shortest bounding wall strictly caps the height.

GOAL: Combine pairs of matching tokens to create larger items, then place the final result inside the target bubble. CONTROLS: Clicking on empty space merges nearby tokens of the same type into a new token centered at the click. RULE: A merge only occurs if the click point is within the effective range of all tokens intended to combine. TRAP: Do not assume tokens merge automatically when they touch; you must actively click the specific location where the new token should appear.

GOAL: Clear the charcoal gate to open the passage for the knob. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the knob; clicks fired the beam. RULE: The beam dissolves the charcoal, creating a wide enough gap for the 4x4 knob to pass through. TRAP: Thinking the beam destroyed the plug; it had no effect on the plug, wasting actions on irrelevant targets.

GOAL: Match each column’s shape to its target key. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP rotates the selected shape. RULE: Every shape cycles through the same seven forms, so rotation steps are fixed. TRAP: Assuming a shape returns to its start after six presses; it actually takes seven.

GOAL: Move both crosses so their arms pass through all matching colored dots. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the active cross; Space switches to the other cross. RULE: Each cross’s center must sit at the intersection of the lines defined by its dots. TRAP: Believing the cross arms must physically touch the dots; they only need to align along the same row or column.

GOAL: Guide two colored dots to land precisely on the center of a central plus symbol. CONTROLS: Click colored panels to extend the matching bar by three units. RULE: Each click extends the bar exactly three spaces; the dot moves with the tip. TRAP: Assuming one click moves the dot one space wastes time; you must click three times per unit of distance.

GOAL: Position each shape so its edges cover all matching colored dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space switches to the next shape. RULE: A shape’s edge covers dots lying exactly on its diagonal lines, including vertices. TRAP: Assuming dots must be inside the shape’s area; they only need to touch the edges.

GOAL: Merge scattered pluses into a single unit using six precise moves. CONTROLS: Clicking a plus moves it to the highlighted cross; colliding pluses vanish. RULE: The cross marks the landing spot where a clicked plus slides until it hits another. TRAP: Believing pluses slide to the board edge; they actually stop immediately upon touching a neighbor.

GOAL: Rotate the ring until the yellow tile sits in the bracket. CONTROLS: Click the left arrow to shift tiles counterclockwise, right arrow for clockwise. RULE: Alignment is the only solution; ignore color patterns elsewhere on the ring. TRAP: Analyzing opposite tile symmetry wastes time; focus solely on the single target position.

GOAL: Move two separate squares into the high archway and bring them together to merge into a single block. CONTROLS: Arrows shift both squares simultaneously in the chosen direction. Space attempts to finalize the move or merge. RULE: Squares move as a rigid pair unless blocked, requiring coordinated paths to navigate narrow vertical gaps. TRAP: Assuming reaching the top area completes the level; you must also slide them horizontally until they touch.

GOAL: Move shapes to cover every dot on the grid exactly once. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the selected piece; Space switches which piece you control. RULE: Overlap is forbidden; each dot must be touched by precisely one shape. TRAP: Assuming shapes could stack or that partial coverage was acceptable wasted time.

GOAL: Place both blocks onto matching sockets to clear the room. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the active block exactly three spaces; clicking a block makes it active. RULE: Only the block with the white dot responds to arrows; the black-dotted block is inert. TRAP: Believing arrows control a fixed player wastes moves; you must click to switch which block is active before moving it.

GOAL: Shrink the rope knot by moving the white diamond next to the gray one. CONTROLS: Click any open space to move the white diamond; click the gray diamond to swap positions. RULE: The knot’s size shrinks as the distance between the two diamonds decreases. TRAP: Believing the knot stays fixed size; moving far away makes it too large to fit the target ring.

GOAL: Make the bottom-right panel match the pattern shown in its center. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggled it between blue and red. RULE: Unlike the other panels, the center acted as a target image, not a live mirror. TRAP: Assuming the center updated dynamically to reflect current state caused wasted clicks trying to sync live.

GOAL: Place two yellow tiles into the fixed target brackets. CONTROLS: Red buttons shift rings or lanes backward; green buttons shift them forward. RULE: Shared tiles move with both the ring and the lane they occupy. TRAP: Assuming moves are independent ignores how shared tiles couple the systems together.

GOAL: Turn specific cells red to match the panel's small reference map. CONTROLS: Clicking a grid cell toggles its color between blue and red. RULE: The tiny center image acts as a target, showing exactly which cells must be red. TRAP: Assuming the center map was static or decorative, rather than the strict solution guide.

ESTABLISHED: The piston cannot reach the box. The legend shape matches the box shape in state 1, but this does not trigger a win. The orange piston cap does not paint the floor. FAILED: Matching the legend to the box shape. Pushing the piston into the box. Moving the piston over the cross button. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching the legend shape to the box shape. CONTROLS: Pressing rotates the legend 90 degrees clockwise. Moving the piston leaves gray cells behind.

GOAL: Match object colors to target zones by visiting color sources before covering dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; Space cycles between the X and plus symbols. RULE: Centering an object on a colored square permanently changes its hue, even after moving away. TRAP: Assuming color reverts when leaving the source square wastes moves; the change is permanent.

GOAL: Move yellow and orange tiles to their target slots. CONTROLS: Red buttons spin rings one way; green buttons spin them the opposite way. RULE: Tiles move together when on the same ring, but can transfer rings at shared intersection points. TRAP: Assuming green is the inverse of red without verifying, which wastes actions if the rotation direction differs.

GOAL: Match the four mini-maps to flip all twelve target cells to orange. CONTROLS: Click an indicator cell to toggle its corresponding three-by-three region. RULE: Each mini-map shows exactly which cells in its region must become orange. TRAP: Assuming the mini-map position matched the region offset without checking the indicator's own cell location.

GOAL: Rotate the legend shape to match the target picture and push the piston into the frame. CONTROLS: Arrows move the piston. The cross rotates the legend shape. RULE: The piston can only enter the frame when the legend shape perfectly matches the target. TRAP: Matching the shape alone does not win; you must physically move the piston into the frame afterward.

GOAL: Remove block C by jumping the yellow peg over C’s peg into an empty space. CONTROLS: Click the board to slide the yellow block; click its peg to select it, then click the highlighted landing spot to jump. RULE: A peg jumps exactly two spaces, removing the jumped-over peg, only if the landing space is clear. TRAP: Assuming the block stops at the target lattice spot; it often slides past, requiring precise manual positioning before jumping.

ESTABLISHED: Entering the socket removes the cap. The head retracts one cell per turn only while a block occupies the socket. The wire redraws when the block leaves. FAILED: Assuming the head retracts immediately or without a block present. Assuming the ghost cannot occupy the socket. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the exit without managing the snake's retraction timing. CONTROLS: Space toggles modes. Arrows move the active block.

GOAL: Deduce hidden colors to paint the grid. CONTROLS: Click cells to cycle through available colors. RULE: Indicator mini-maps show which cells match the indicator's center color versus which do not. TRAP: Assuming white means "unknown" instead of "matches center" wastes clicks testing redundant possibilities.

GOAL: Match yellow and orange tiles to their colored brackets. CONTROLS: Click arrows to shift ring rows or columns. RULE: Clicking an arrow rotates the entire adjacent ring in that direction. TRAP: Assuming tiles move independently; they always shift together as a ring segment.

GOAL: Navigate past a retracting snake barrier to reach the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the blue block; SPACE activates a switch. RULE: The snake’s head disappears one turn after any block rests on its cap. TRAP: Waiting by moving up and down wastes actions; stand still on the cap to advance time efficiently.

GOAL: Align the plug’s prongs with the socket pins. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the plug horizontally or vertically. RULE: The level completes when prongs touch the pins without overlap. TRAP: Believing you must push the plug fully into the socket, causing a collision.

GOAL: Place pieces to match the target row using two ports and one blue box. CONTROLS: Drag pieces to slots, then press Space to submit. RULE: Both ports must read the same three-piece blue sequence that matches the target. TRAP: Assuming ports could read different sequences or trying to solve them independently.

GOAL: Align the black piece with the yellow target shape. CONTROLS: Arrows moved pieces three cells per step. RULE: Crossing the blue line mirrored the piece's orientation. TRAP: Assuming pieces move one cell per action wasted time.

GOAL: Arrange colored ports in the main box to match the target sequence of nested colors. CONTROLS: Click a tray piece, then click a slot to place it; press space to confirm the solution. RULE: The first item in each three-piece group must match the pre-placed piece of that specific box. TRAP: Placing ports in the target color order instead of matching the pre-placed pieces' box types.

GOAL: Paint specific cells pink while keeping others green to match hidden constraints. CONTROLS: Click empty cells to paint them pink; click marked cells to brush their neighbors. RULE: Brush markers indicate cells that must be pink, not constraints on the center view. TRAP: Assuming brush overlays were constraints; they were just indicators for which cells to paint.

GOAL: Move two yellow tiles onto the matching brackets at the top corners. CONTROLS: Red and green arrows rotate the entire outer ring, while separate top arrows rotate only the top row. RULE: The large ring shifts all tiles one step, but the top row can be adjusted independently without disturbing the rest of the path. TRAP: Assuming the top row moves only with the big ring wastes moves; use the specific top arrows to fine-tune positions after aligning the ring.

GOAL: Move the knob to the blue socket after clearing the path with a laser beam. CONTROLS: Arrows move the knob; clicks fire the laser pattern. RULE: The laser dissolves obstacles, allowing the knob to pass through previously blocked areas. TRAP: Thinking the green square was a key to collect; it was actually an obstacle that the knob could simply push through or bypass.

GOAL: Rotate six columns to match a specific pattern of shapes. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the selection cursor and rotated the current column. RULE: Each column had a unique target shape; the correct rotation was the one that perfectly aligned the pattern. TRAP: Assuming all columns shared the same rotation direction or target orientation wasted many moves.

GOAL: Place ports and pieces so the output sequence is R, b, N, Y, N, b, R. CONTROLS: Drag items to slots. Space confirms the solution. RULE: Ports redirect the sequence, causing nested boxes to expand into the final list. TRAP: Placing the green port directly in red slot 3 breaks the count; it must hide inside the blue box.

GOAL: Rotate each column's pattern to its specific target code. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the active column; RIGHT moves the selection bracket. RULE: Patterns cycle through a fixed orbit; count steps to reach the target. TRAP: Assuming the bracket stays put; it wraps around, so check its position before rotating.

GOAL: Align the charcoal block precisely over the yellow zone to complete the level. CONTROLS: Arrows move the currently highlighted piece; Space toggles which piece is active. RULE: Only the piece with white dots responds to arrow keys; the other remains stationary. TRAP: Assuming Space moves the piece itself rather than just switching control between pieces.

ESTABLISHED: The podium is a static T-shape. The red fill sits inside the white frame, not perfectly centered, suggesting the frame is a socket with extra space. FAILED: Interpreting the podium as a directional arrow or dial setting yielded no progress. GOAL IS NOT: The T-shape is not a code for a dial position or a directional instruction. CONTROLS: Clicking the podium did nothing. Interacting with the frame/fill relationship is the untested key.

GOAL: Align the yellow connector’s pins with the green bar while pairing the purple plug to its remaining ports. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shifted the selected piece three units per press; clicking selected the purple plug. RULE: A connection formed only when red tips perfectly overlapped, turning gray to confirm the link. TRAP: Moving the yellow piece inadvertently broke the existing purple connection, forcing a separate realignment.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking blocks destroys them or opens columns. The bubble rises when blocks above are removed. Arrow keys move the blue character. FAILED: Moving the character into the shaft did not make the bubble descend. Clicking empty space did nothing. GOAL IS NOT: Simply navigating the blue character to an exit. CONTROLS: Click blocks to clear paths. Arrow keys move the blue character.

ESTABLISHED: The canvas is a fixed 10x10 block with an immovable white top and purple bottom. FAILED: Moving the canvas with UP/DOWN keys and pressing to shift it have both proven ineffective. GOAL IS NOT: Achieving a half-white, half-purple pattern by moving the canvas up or down. CONTROLS: UP and DOWN do not move the canvas; SPACE presses the stamp to paint or interact without shifting blocks.

GOAL: Guide the player to the exit while evading a patrolling orange guard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step; the guard moves automatically each turn. RULE: Only sharing the exact same cell causes death, allowing safe movement along adjacent paths. TRAP: Assuming proximity triggers a game over wastes time; ignoring distance lets you slip past safely.

GOAL: Place three yellow tiles into the central cross's inner slots. CONTROLS: Click arm centers to rotate or shift tiles along that arm; click the center to swap inner and outer positions across all arms. RULE: The center swap is the only way to move tiles from the outer arms into the required inner slots. TRAP: Assuming rotations alone could reach the goal wastes moves; you must use the center swap to transfer tiles inward.

GOAL: Clear the maze by timing your arrival at the exit after allies secure the path. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character; Spacebar confirms the start of the timed sequence. RULE: The exit only opens after an ally reaches the target, requiring you to delay your final approach. TRAP: Moving straight to the exit without pausing causes you to get stuck against the closed gate.

GOAL: Move both colored knots to their matching rings. CONTROLS: Click a knot to move it; click a gem to swap colors. RULE: A knot sits exactly where two gems of the same color meet. TRAP: Thinking you can move a knot without first aligning its source gems.

GOAL: Guide the bubble to the pink exit marker. CONTROLS: Arrows move horizontally; clicking carves a temporary vertical shaft. RULE: The bubble rises through carved openings and closes behind it. TRAP: Thinking the shaft stays open; you must re-carve to rise again.

GOAL: Position moving pieces so their reflections perfectly cover the yellow target shapes. CONTROLS: Arrows move the currently active object; Space switches which object is active. RULE: Pieces move normally, but their mirror images appear inverted above the horizontal center line. TRAP: Dot colors change when overlapping targets, masking the active piece indicator; ignore colors and test moves to identify the active object.

GOAL: Navigate to the goal while avoiding moving orange obstacles. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step per turn; time advances automatically with each move. RULE: Obstacles patrol fixed lanes in repeating cycles; you must predict their positions to find safe gaps. TRAP: Assuming obstacles stay still or move randomly leads to collisions; they follow strict, predictable paths.

GOAL: Move both yellow tiles into the marked bracket slots. CONTROLS: Click row arrows to shift tiles horizontally; click column arrows to shift vertically. RULE: Rotating a 2x2 block moves corner tiles clockwise, allowing precise placement without disturbing other rows. TRAP: Assuming rotations are reversible by simple clicks; reversing requires inverse moves, not just clicking the opposite arrow.

GOAL: Dissolve specific maze blocks to clear the exit path. CONTROLS: Arrows move the knob; cross clicks grow or shrink it; L clicks warp between frames. RULE: Warp preserves your relative position within the active frame, not absolute grid coordinates. TRAP: Believing warp moves you to a fixed spot wastes time; track your offset instead.

GOAL: Move the white piece to clear the final obstacle. CONTROLS: Click a diamond to move the white piece toward it. RULE: Clicks only register if the target is within a five-by-five square of the diamond. TRAP: Assuming clicks worked in a diamond shape; they actually work in a square, causing missed moves.

GOAL: Cover four scattered blue dots with a plus-shaped piece without touching red or blue square zones. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plus piece one step at a time. RULE: The plus must align its center to cover all four dots simultaneously while staying clear of forbidden areas. TRAP: Assuming the plus could cover distant dots with its arms alone; precise center alignment is required for full coverage.

GOAL: Align three distinct shapes into specific target zones without overlapping. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the currently selected piece; Space cycled selection between the bar and two blocks. RULE: Only the piece with white highlights responds to input; others stay still until selected. TRAP: Mistaking static yellow cells for active white highlights, causing wasted moves on the wrong piece.

GOAL: Align the plunger with the gap and insert it to finish. CONTROLS: Click bars to raise fluid levels; click the orange plug to move the plunger. RULE: The plug activates only when fluid surfaces exactly meet the plug's bottom edge. TRAP: Assuming the plunger fits through the gap if body rows align; only the tail must match the gap's height.

GOAL: Align the horizontal bar, vertical bar, and yellow piece to their target markers. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected object; Space cycles selection between the horizontal bar, vertical bar, and piece. RULE: Only one object is active at a time, marked by white dashes; the others remain stationary. TRAP: Assuming both bars could move simultaneously or misidentifying the active bar due to dashes at their intersection.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding charging guards. CONTROLS: Arrows move one step. RULE: Guards charge straight ahead; approach only from the side or back to capture them safely. TRAP: Assuming any adjacent cell is safe ignores the guard's facing direction, leading to instant death.

GOAL: Tile the blue hex row with domino rules to match the pink target row. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selection cursor to choose which domino applies next. RULE: Domino inputs must match the blue row as non-contiguous subsequences, not just adjacent pairs. TRAP: Believing chunks had to be strictly contiguous in the row, causing endless failed tiling attempts.

ESTABLISHED: The level is currently stuck with insufficient pieces to form the required 3x3 shape. FAILED: Merging mixed colors, clicking goal markers, and waiting for token respawns produced no results. GOAL IS NOT: Achievable through standard merging of the remaining Y and M tokens alone. CONTROLS: Clicking triggers ripple effects; moving tokens consumes bar cells; no action drains the bar to reset.

GOAL: Reach the exit by traveling from the bottom-left corner to the top-right area, then dropping down to the final cell. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step; walls block movement while grass allows passage. RULE: Guards only threaten specific lines, allowing safe passage if you avoid their direct paths. TRAP: Assuming you must fight or capture the guard blocking the side path wastes turns when a clear route exists along the top edge.

GOAL: Move both snakes to their exit gaps by swapping them between tanks. CONTROLS: Arrows raise or lower water levels in specific tanks; plugs swap snakes when adjacent tanks match height. RULE: Equal water levels in neighboring tanks allow a plug click to transfer the snake across. TRAP: Assuming a snake stays put during a swap; it moves to the adjacent tank, requiring new height adjustments for its next step.

GOAL: Align two separate blocks into a single connected shape. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the entire structure until it hits a wall. RULE: Blocks sharing an edge are considered one piece and move together. TRAP: Believing blocks pass through each other; they actually merge upon contact.

GOAL: Align three distinct shapes to cover all yellow target squares. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; Space switches to the next piece. RULE: Switch pieces before moving to ensure you act on the correct shape. TRAP: Moving immediately after switching often wastes actions if the wrong piece is active; verify the selection first.

GOAL: Slide all four blocks into their matching holes. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active block; clicks select a new block. RULE: Only the currently selected block responds to arrow inputs. TRAP: Forgetting to click a block before moving it wastes actions.

ESTABLISHED: Fourteen pegs exist across four groups. A thirteen-jump sequence reduces them to one. The board scrolls vertically to reveal hidden pegs. FAILED: Counting fifteen pegs or assuming a twelve-jump path. Ignoring off-screen pegs initially. GOAL IS NOT: Clearing all pegs instantly. Leaving two or more pegs behind. CONTROLS: Click a peg, then a landing spot to jump over an adjacent peg, removing the jumped one.

ESTABLISHED: Yellow gate at (20,50) opens on pulse; caps at (32,38), (50,20), (20,32) retract heads; target at (20,20). FAILED: Direct routing requires 46 moves, exceeding the ~41 move budget; simple pathing fails to save enough steps. GOAL IS NOT: A simple race to the target; it is a puzzle of optimizing move count via ghost recording. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move; SPACE records/replays ghost in slots; ghost paths block or assist depending on timing.

GOAL: Guide the pair to the target while avoiding the orange. CONTROLS: Arrows moved both pieces together in that direction. RULE: The pair moves as one rigid unit, sharing walls and bounds. TRAP: Trying to block or push the orange failed; it ignores you, so you must dodge its path entirely.

ESTABLISHED: The left demo shows four up-stroke glyphs in the bottom row move the piece up sixteen pixels. FAILED: Mixing directions in a single row cancels movement, and row-major execution models failed to predict results. GOAL IS NOT: A lateral or downward shift; the piece must rise to meet the overhead cavity. CONTROLS: Clicking grid cells toggles glyph types. The run button executes the sequence left-to-right, bottom-row only.

GOAL: Slide the player piece around obstacles to push colored blocks into matching holes. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; walking into a block pushes it one space. RULE: Blocks slide straight until hitting a wall or another block; the player must stand on the opposite side to push. TRAP: Assuming blocks stop after one space; they slide far, so plan the final landing spot before pushing.

ESTABLISHED: A single stream touches all containers, but the level does not clear. FAILED: Simultaneous contact with all three notches via one shot; filling the gray ceiling area. GOAL IS NOT: Touching all containers in one go, or simply filling the top region. CONTROLS: SPACE fires the fluid; RIGHT moves the source; UNDO reverses the last action.

GOAL: You must cover every highlighted tile by placing two bars and two blocks. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; space selects a new one. RULE: Each piece covers only one row or column orbit, so align them carefully to hit all targets. TRAP: Assuming you can cover multiple orbits with one block wastes moves; focus on single-orbit precision first.

ESTABLISHED: The purple vertical bar is a fixed wall. The plus sign is located to the right of this wall. The player object has caps and dots, unlike the wall. FAILED: Pushing the purple wall up or down. Attempting to move the dot through the wall. Assuming the plus sign is not behind the wall. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving the dot to the plus sign if the wall is truly impassable. The wall is not a pushable object like the player's bars. CONTROLS: Clicking coordinates moves the player or attempts to push adjacent objects. No-op actions halt batched command sequences. The purple bar does not respo

ESTABLISHED: The win triggers on the last plug move, not full mating. Two connectors remain red in the victory state. FAILED: Trying to mate every connector before moving the final piece. Waiting for a "all gray" state stalls the level. GOAL IS NOT: A fully mated network. The victory condition ignores specific unmated red blocks on the white object. CONTROLS: Clicking a plug moves it. The level completes immediately upon placing the final piece, regardless of remaining red connections.

ESTABLISHED: The bubble floats in the pocket at rows 37-42. Purple hazards kill on contact. Water fills carved spaces but may heal over time. FAILED: The bubble died when it rose into a pocket with purple directly above it. GOAL IS NOT: The goal is not to reach the purple blocks or the room below. CONTROLS: Carve to open paths. The bubble rises through water and moves into newly carved adjacent spaces.

GOAL: Move the yellow square fully inside the blue zone. CONTROLS: Click to slide the square; distance must stay under six units. RULE: Only moves with gaps under six succeed; larger jumps fail silently. TRAP: Assuming long diagonal hops save time; they exceed the limit and waste clicks.

GOAL: Clear the row by engulfing the Right, North, and blue block into the extending arm. CONTROLS: Left and Right extend or retract the arm; Up and Down move the arm vertically. RULE: The arm pushes adjacent blocks until they hit a wall or another block, then engulfs them upon extension. TRAP: Believing you must move the arm vertically first; extending horizontally in row zero clears the path efficiently.

GOAL: Rotate three plugs so their connectors face matching ports on the frame, then slide them into place. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected plug; Space rotates it ninety degrees clockwise. RULE: A joint connects only when two facing plugs point directly at each other. TRAP: Assuming Space moves the piece; it only rotates, requiring extra arrow presses to reposition.

ESTABLISHED: Reaching zero energy is safe; only acting at zero fails. Covering a ring refills energy to eighty-four. Walls remain static. FAILED: Previous plans assumed the piston stayed fixed at its old location, ignoring its new position at the start. GOAL IS NOT: A fixed target location. The goal moves with the piston, requiring dynamic pathing. CONTROLS: Directions move the character. Moving into a ring consumes it and refills energy. Moving into the piston pushes it.

GOAL: Move the piston five steps down to push the ring into the box. CONTROLS: Down arrow moves the piston; each step costs energy. RULE: Touching a ring refills energy, but only if you have enough left to reach it. TRAP: Assuming the bar stays high enough; it drops faster than expected, leaving barely enough for one final move.
GOAL: Shrink the yellow box to free the green dot. CONTROLS: Click panel to grow or shrink the box. RULE: Left panel shrinks, right panel grows. TRAP: Assuming all panels shrink the box wastes time.

GOAL: Clear stray marks, then paint the bottom rows purple. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the stamp; Space applies the selected color; Clicks pick the color. RULE: The 135-degree stamp covers the lower-left half, clearing all existing marks at once. TRAP: Thinking you must clear marks individually; using the wrong diagonal stamp leaves marks behind.

GOAL: Reach the yellow window on the gray block. CONTROLS: Arrows move the token; mouse clicks flip the blue square's position and the arm's direction. RULE: The token can only stand on open space or the blue square, never on gray walls or the arm. TRAP: Thinking the blue square must be moved before moving the token; the token can start directly on the blue square's current location.

GOAL: Stamp purple, white, and orange regions to complete the picture. CONTROLS: Arrows orbit the stamp around the canvas; clicks select ink; space applies it. RULE: Diagonal and side positions stamp specific triangular or rectangular zones, requiring precise placement. TRAP: Assuming down moves are blocked at diagonals wastes time; they often slide the stamp along the edge.

GOAL: Extend the arm to hit the target without breaking the chain. CONTROLS: Arrows move the arm; Right extends, Left retracts. RULE: Extending shifts the entire contiguous block of segments attached to the tip, not just the tip itself. TRAP: Thinking retraction moves only the tip; it actually pulls the whole connected run, leaving gaps if segments aren't touching.
